why: Every arm in this campaign pinned the non-expert organ at 4 bits / group 64. It costs 0.4318 complete EBPW alone -- 43% of a 1.0 target -- so it put an unexamined floor under every result. This probes it.
RESULT_the_non_expert_organ_CANNOT_be_ch: Not by bits: 3b/g128 gives ppl 3.714 (gate 3.617) and 4-gram 0.5484 (gate 0.1614); 2b/g128 destroys the model at ppl 19398. Not by group either: 4b/g128 IMPROVES perplexity to 3.087 -- better than the passing baseline's 3.135 -- and still FAILS on generation at 0.2903. Every reduction attempted fails, so 0.4318 EBPW is a MEASURED hard floor, not an assumption.
THE_STRUCTURAL_ASYMMETRY: Experts are 90.2% of the weights and tolerate 16 -> 3.25 bits (4.9x) while still passing. Non-experts are 9.8% and break on a further 4.5 -> 3.25 (1.4x). Precision sensitivity runs OPPOSITE to byte share on this specimen. Attention, router, embed and lm_head are the fragile organ and they are the one nobody was compressing.
CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_1p0_TARGET: With the non-expert organ fixed at its floor of 0.4318, a 1.0 complete EBPW target leaves 0.5682 for 14.4B expert weights = 0.3157 bits/weight. Not 1 bit. Not 0.65. About 0.32 -- which no quantiser reaches, and which requires removing weights (sparsity), sharing them, or replacing them with a generator.
PERPLEXITY_AND_GENERATION_DISSOCIATE_AGA: 4b/g128 has BETTER perplexity than the passing baseline and fails on generation. That is the FOURTH instance on this specimen, after q2-g128 (ppl 4.085 with 87 identical tokens), q4-g128 vs q3-g128, and residual-binary vs affine. Perplexity alone would have accepted at least three of these. The generation term is not a refinement of the gate, it is load-bearing.
